title: Installing a Whole-House Water Filter with Push-Fit Fittings (This Old House)

locations.name: Garage mechanical room
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly identifies the corner of the garage as the mechanical room and describes mounting and piping there

locations.name: Street curb stop valve and meter pit
locations.basis: Transcript describes turning water off at the curb stop by the street and mentions a meter pit with two meters

summary: The video details the installation of a whole-house water filter in a garage mechanical room. It covers selecting between two cartridge types (dirt/rust and dirt/rust plus chlorine removal) to address chlorine taste, mounting the filter on a plywood-backed bracket, and modifying the plumbing with push-fit (solderless) fittings and adapters from 1 inch to 3/4 inch. The host explains shutting off water at the street curb stop, creating isolation on both sides of the filter with two shut-off valves, and grounding considerations after adding the filter. A test run follows to check for leaks, and maintenance guidance notes cartridge replacement every 2–3 months.

sections.title: Intro: Cartridge options and plan
concepts: Cartridge options: dirt/rust vs dirt/rust + chlorine removal
Filter cartridge placement within the housing
sections.description: The video opens by presenting the two cartridge options and selecting chlorine-removal due to chlorine taste concerns, then describes how the cartridge sits inside the clear filter housing.

sections.title: Water path through the filter and where to shut off
concepts: Water enters filter from city supply
Filtered water returns to the building
sections.description: Water flow is described: cold water from the city goes into the filter housing, passes through the cartridge, and exits back into the building.

sections.title: Curb stop shut-off and plan for isolation
concepts: Public-water shut-off at street curb stop
Two isolation valves to isolate filter
sections.description: The host explains where to shut off the water at the street (curb stop) and introduces the idea of using two shut-off valves on either side of the filter to simplify service.

sections.title: Push-fit fittings: a solderless connection overview
sections.description: A demonstration of push-fit fittings shows the internal O-ring and stainless teeth that grip the pipe when pushed in about 1 inch, providing a watertight seal without soldering.

sections.title: Bracket mounting and sizing connections
concepts: 1-inch to 3/4-inch adapter and initial Teflon tape prep
sections.description: A plywood backing is mounted to create a sturdy base for the filter bracket, and the team discusses using a 1-inch to 3/4-inch adapter with PTFE tape on threads.

sections.title: Thread preparation and final tightening
sections.description: The presenter emphasizes applying PTFE tape, threading connections fully, and using witness marks to ensure full seating of the push-fit and threaded fittings.

sections.title: Pipe prep and cutting guidance
sections.description: Instructions cover cutting the pipe, avoiding kinks in the cut, and cleaning the cut ends with emery cloth before fitting.

sections.title: Starting the street-to-filter connections
concepts: Supply pipe from street to filter
Witness marks to verify seating depth
sections.description: Connections from the street to the filter are assembled. The team pushes fittings into place, checking seating depth with witness marks and preparing the run toward the house.

sections.title: Completing downstream connections and isolation valves
sections.description: The downstream connections are completed using push-fit fittings, with attention to two isolation shut-offs and preparing the ground bonding path around the meter.

sections.title: System repressurization and leak check
sections.description: Water is repressurized and checked for leaks. The host and assistant verify there are no leaks as the system pressurizes.

sections.title: Cartridge maintenance planning
sections.description: The video notes that cartridge maintenance should occur every 2–3 months and mentions the included wrench to facilitate changes.

sections.title: Wrap-up and final notes
sections.description: A brief closing segment wraps up the installation and notes the final checks and status of the system.
